proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a short series, leading to unstable peak height/width across rolling windows.
proposals.rationale: Primary hospitalization-aligned branch: explicit H compartment matches target semantics and can better capture sharp peaks via an admission state without mixing incidence into the observation.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-flexibility from fractional dynamics can amplify rolling-split instability and distort peak timing/decay if parameters are weakly identified.
proposals.rationale: Fractional counterpart to test whether heavy-tailed/slow-decay dynamics improve fit to high-peakiness hospitalization waves while keeping observation strictly hospitalization-aligned.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Observation-map mismatch (I proxy vs true admissions) may still bias amplitude/shape; delay may not be constant across the season.
proposals.rationale: Lag-focused control with reduced flexibility: keeps waning/reinfection for recurrent-wave shape while using a 2-week delay consistent with prior delay sensitivity and hospitalization lag semantics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Parameter non-identifiability can cause rolling variability; fractional terms may overfit local peak structure even with correct lag.
proposals.rationale: Direct continuation of the discovered family but shifting to the empirically favored lag; fractional dynamics may help match sharp peaks while maintaining the 2-week phase alignment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is closer to 2 weeks, delay=3 will phase-shift peaks late and degrade short-horizon forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Explore longer clinical/reporting lag as a primary timing alternative for older-age hospitalization series; retains waning to support recurrent-wave dynamics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Compounded flexibility (fractional + longer delay) may increase timing uncertainty and rolling instability, especially around peak weeks.
proposals.rationale: Longer-lag fractional variant to test whether added memory plus 3-week delay better matches steep rise and slower decline in high-rate older-age hospitalizations.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Likely phase misalignment (too-short lag) causing early-peaking forecasts and systematic timing error near the seasonal maximum.
proposals.rationale: Baseline/control lag per constraints: non-fractional version to isolate whether prior poor performance at delay=1 was driven by fractional over-flexibility versus true phase misalignment.
